name: Grafana Labs (formerly Raintank)
subcategory: observability (Grafana, Loki, Mimir, Tempo, Pyroscope, k6)
origin_detail: Torkel Ödegaard released Grafana in January 2014, growing out of Graphite work at Orbitz, with a UI originally based on Kibana 3. The company was founded in 2014 as Raintank and later renamed Grafana Labs; Raj Dutt (CEO) and Ödegaard are co-founders. HQ city not confirmed in fetched pages.
openness_notes: Grafana was Apache-2.0. In April 2021 Grafana, Loki and Tempo were relicensed to AGPL-3.0, an OSI-approved copyleft licence; plugins, agents and some libraries stayed Apache-2.0. Revenue comes from Grafana Cloud and enterprise features, so open core (2), but the core remains OSI open source.

license_history.license: AGPL-3.0 (Grafana, Loki, Tempo; later Mimir, Pyroscope, k6); Apache-2.0 for plugins, agents, some libraries
license_history.note: Announced by Raj Dutt, blog dated 2021-04-20/21; CLA switched to one based on the ASF CLA.

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Stayed OSI-approved; Grafana presented AGPL as a middle path versus peers' moves to non-OSI source-available licences. No fork found.

robustness: VC-backed single vendor, but the core projects stay OSI-licensed (AGPL), so a fork remains legally possible. It acquires and folds in projects (k6 2021, Pyroscope 2023) and in 2025 donated Beyla to OpenTelemetry.
openness_effect_assessment: Grafana tightened from Apache-2.0 to AGPL in 2021 instead of adopting SSPL or BSL, keeping the open-source label. Growth continued: the valuation went from $3B (Series C, August 2021) to over $6B (August 2024), ARR passed $250M and paying customers rose from 2,000 (2022) to over 5,000 (2024). Copyleft appears to have deterred hosted free-riding without the trust costs Elastic and Redis paid.
key_takeaway: Grafana Labs is the main counter-example in this group: it chose an OSI copyleft licence over a source-available one, avoided any fork, and kept compounding its private valuation (over $6B in 2024). Elastic (2024) and Redis (2025) later re-added AGPL themselves, which makes Grafana's 2021 choice look like where the relicensing wave settled.
